title: What can I paste into a work AI?
summary: Decide whether sharing is allowed. Then make a small copy that still answers the question.

intro.what: Start with the rules for the training workspace. Make the smallest copy that can answer the question.
intro.features: Check every field before you share. Write down what you sent and why.
intro.exchange: Keep the link between a mail retry and a delivery while removing real addresses.
intro.m365: Check the allowed account and workspace before you share a marked document.
intro.developer: Use fake project settings when asking for help with a broken app.
sources: Microsoft Learn · sensitivity labels and data policies
Microsoft Learn · scope of enterprise data protection

sections.title: Check the permission before the paste
paragraphs: Open the practice kit, then its cases folder. Read SP1 through SP4 in share-policy.txt. Find the allowed tool and task. Hold the request if the rule gives no clear yes.
sources: Microsoft Learn · sensitivity labels and data policies
Microsoft Learn · scope of enterprise data protection

sections.title: Build a new excerpt from the facts you need
paragraphs: Open share-draft.txt on your own device. Start a clean note. Keep the order, the time gap, the source labels and the result. Use Box A in both rows. Use Relay A and Relay B for the two sources. Keep the label key on your device.
sources: Microsoft Learn · sensitivity labels and data policies

sections.title: Stop secret values at the source
paragraphs: A secret can let someone use an account. Leave its value out of the note, files, images and logs. If a real secret was shared, stop. Tell the owner through an approved channel. Follow the steps to revoke or replace it.

sections.title: Leave a receipt for the decision
paragraphs: Record the date, place, purpose and kinds of fields. List what you took out. If you held the request, write “nothing sent.” For a share, list what went out and who could read it. Follow the work rule for keeping the log.
sources: Microsoft Learn · sensitivity labels and data policies
Microsoft Learn · scope of enterprise data protection

exercise.prompt: Your manager says to hurry, but the data class of a project nickname is unknown. The nickname is not needed. What is your next move?
answer: Drop the nickname locally and check that the remaining fields and destination are allowed. If any part of the remaining packet or destination is unclear, hold the request for the policy owner.

wordHelp: alias
A made-up label that stands in for a name or address.
redaction
Taking private details out of a copy before sharing it.
hold
Pause the task until the missing proof or permission arrives.
evidence
A line, file or test result that you can check.
permission
A rule that says who may do what.

title: When the pasted note tries to give orders
summary: Keep a reader’s request separate from instructions copied inside a ticket, message or document.

intro.what: A note may contain an order as well as a fact. Read the order as part of the note.
intro.features: Look for the entry made by the person who can close the case.
intro.exchange: Keep a quoted mail footer from changing the conclusion of a mail case.
intro.m365: Read a pasted meeting note without treating an old request as approval.
intro.developer: Stop a feedback summary from changing an app setting because of words in a comment.
sources: Microsoft Learn · untrusted document content and prompt injection

sections.title: Draw the boundary on the page
paragraphs: Your task in share-note.txt is a read-only summary. Cover SN5 for the first run. Underline the status on SN1, then circle the instruction-like words in SN3. SN3 is text copied from a form footer. It gives no authority to act and records no outcome.

Ask the helper for the last recorded state, a supporting line and the missing proof. Label the excerpt as data. Use a context that has no ability to change a ticket for this reading task. Quotation marks make the boundary easier to read. They cannot guarantee a model will respect it.
sources: Microsoft Learn · untrusted document content and prompt injection

sections.title: Check what the reply claims
paragraphs: With SN1 through SN4, expect Open and pending confirmation. If the reply says Closed, look for a dated status change or authorized state event. The note has neither in this first run. Reject the claim and record the bad inference before accepting a new summary.

Now add SN5 as a later event. Closed is supported in this second run because the analyst recorded it after confirmation. The copied footer is still only evidence of words someone put on a form. Leave the actual case system alone in both runs.
sources: Microsoft Learn · untrusted document content and prompt injection

exercise.prompt: Both SN3 and SN5 use a form of the word close. Which one can support a state change in the second summary?
answer: SN5 reports a completed event. SN3 requests action inside a quoted footer. A word match alone cannot decide the state.

sections.title: Log the boundary you tested
paragraphs: In a practice log, write that the input was a scrubbed, fictional status excerpt and the output was a read-only summary. Record the source line that supported the state and whether you held back the correction until SN5 arrived. A log can describe an instruction-like footer without copying its raw contents or any identities.
sources: Microsoft Learn · untrusted document content and prompt injection
Microsoft Learn · sensitivity labels and data policies
